articles.title: Banded Rows
articles.summary: Soft horizontal metallic/roughness bands with feathered transitions, very low coverage, subtle. Reads as a smooth sheen with a very faint linear grain; the bands are too fine to see as bands.
articles.what: Adds horizontal metallic/roughness bands with soft feathered transitions between value zones Up close: Extremely fine regular dotted lines about 8 px apart that run as faint vertical ticks in this crop, with soft gradual feathering. On satin there is almost nothing; on metal a delicate fine ribbed texture shows inside the lit band. From a distance: Reads as a smooth sheen with a very faint linear grain; the bands are too fine to see as bands. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Structure & Geometry (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Structure & Geometry", or search for "Banded Rows".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood and roof on a metallic base
Skip matte panels, nothing shows
No effect on numbers.
Practically invisible
Pairs well with: matte, satin, metallic.
pitfalls: Not racing stripes: the name says bands but at this scale they are hairline ribbing
Not brushed metal: it is regular and dotted, not random strands
Avoid: chrome, gloss.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.
